title: Release manifest of tools/release/build-release-set.ps1
description: One row per component build of a release set. build_release_set.py validates every manifest against this file before it plans anything, so this schema is the contract and the tool has no second copy of it.

release.description: The release name, for example tester.32.

version.description: The package version that {version} gives every recipe that stamps a version resource. -Version replaces it.

recipe_repository.description: The name of this repository in 'repositories'.

recipe_commit.description: The commit of this repository whose recipes build every row of another repository that names no recipe_commit of its own. A row of this repository takes the recipe of its own commit, as provenance.py reads a row without recipe_commit.

repositories.description: The table of release-sources.json (url, checkouts, submodules), and the base of the attribution scan of each repository.

sentence.description: A reason a person can use: at least 40 characters and 6 words, the rule of provenance.py for 'unverified'.

base.description: The commit the attribution scan starts from (exclusive): usually the commit the previous release pinned.

file.description: The file under {out} that the build writes.

path.description: The package path it ships as: the 'path' of its release-sources.json row.

flavour.description: The flavour of its release-sources.json row, when it is not the build's (the INF of the release KMD is 'shared').

component.description: The component of its release-sources.json row, when it is not the build's (one hosted ICD build ships in the D3D12 and the D3D11 slot).

unsigned.description: The image under {out} before the build signed it: the row gets its unsigned_sha256.

authenticode.description: true: the release signs this file again, so the row gets its authenticode_sha256 and the package copy is compared by that digest.

release_edits.description: Copied to the row: what build-release.ps1 changes in the packaged copy.

pair_skew.description: Copied to the row: why this wow64 file and its x64 pair come from different commits.

run.description: A .ps1, .py or .exe. A relative path is a file of the recipe tree; placeholders as in args.

requires.description: A path (placeholders as in args): the test runs only when it exists, and the report says why it did not.

summary.description: A regular expression with named groups (checks, failures, skipped, ...). Each matching line of the test's output adds its numbers to the report.

pass.description: A regular expression that at least one line of the output must match, in addition to exit code 0.

id.description: Short: the build directory is <work>\<id>, and Mesa's deep paths need a short prefix.

base.description: The start of this row's attribution scan, in place of the repository's base.

tree.description: worktree (default): a work tree of its own. shared: one read-only work tree for every row of this repository and commit, which must still be clean after the build. clone: a new repository (BuildTree.psm1 New-Tree -Clone).

compiler.description: Named for every row: no build falls back to a compiler without a word.

compiler_reason.description: Why a user-mode row builds with msvc: compatibility, correctness or a measured advantage.

deterministic.description: true: the recipe claims a bit-identical rebuild. false: 'unverified' says why not.

disk_peak_gb.description: The most this build occupies at once, its own trees included and shared trees not. Default 2.

slots.description: How many of -MaxParallel the build takes, at most all of them (then it runs alone); its {jobs} are slots times the jobs of one slot. Default 1.

keep.description: Further files under {out} that the artifact keeps (recipe.json is always kept when the build writes one).
